## 1 Overview

Formalize offers built-in AI capabilities that assist users in their compliance work. Two capabilities are available today: SmartFill, which suggests values for form fields by reading documents
the user selects; and Formalize IQ, an AI assistant that works across your live governance,
risk, and compliance program - analysing your records, surfacing gaps, answering questions,
and, when a user explicitly asks, drafting and connecting records or building dashboards. It
can also work on files - a spreadsheet, a PDF, a Word document, whether attached to the conversation or already held in the workspace - by running code in an isolated sandbox, and look
up public sources such as regulations and standards through a search service that runs inside
AWS. Every action Formalize IQ takes on your data is reviewed and approved by a human and
recorded in the audit trail.

All AI capabilities run on the same infrastructure and follow the same security principles as the
rest of the platform, with the additional safeguards described in this document. AI is controlled
per organisation: it can be disabled at any time from within the platform, and on request we
remove the AI feature from an organisation entirely, so that it cannot be enabled at all.

This document focuses on the AI capabilities specifically. The platform’s general security measures, such as architecture, encryption, access management, and vulnerability management,
are described in our Security Whitepaper, which is available upon request.

## 2 Definitions

The following terms are used throughout this document:

• **Model:** A large language model: software trained on large amounts of text to understand
and generate language. The models used by Formalize are pre-trained, general-purpose
models developed by Anthropic.

• **Prompt:** The input sent to the model for a single request - for example, the documents
and field definitions SmartFill reads, or the records and instructions Formalize IQ works
from.

• **Completion:** The output the model returns for a prompt - for example, SmartFill’s suggested values, or Formalize IQ’s answer or proposed action.

• **Inference:** The act of running a model on a prompt to produce a completion. Inference
is stateless: the model does not remember anything between requests.

• **General-purpose AI model:** An AI model capable of performing a wide range of tasks,
as defined in the EU AI Act. The Claude models used by Formalize are general-purpose
AI models.

• **Amazon Bedrock:** An AWS-managed service that runs AI models from multiple developers entirely within AWS infrastructure. The model developer has no access to the data
processed by the service.

---

• **Agent:** An AI capability that completes multi-step tasks by calling well-defined tools,
always bound by the requesting user’s permissions. Formalize IQ is built on agents.

• **Tool:** A well-defined, single-purpose function an agent can call - for example, to look
up records the user has access to or to draft a new record. Every tool call is checked
against the requesting user’s permissions, and tools that change data additionally require
the user’s approval.

• **Sandbox:** An isolated, temporary computing environment in which an agent can run
code, with no route to the public internet, to our network, or to the platform. Formalize
uses a sandbox that is provided and operated by AWS.

• **Prompt injection:** An attack in which instructions are hidden inside content an AI reads
- a document, a web page, a form answer - in an attempt to make it act against the user’s
intent. The safeguards against it are described under Formalize IQ.

## 3 Controls at a Glance

The table below summarises the key facts and controls described in this document:

| Control | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Capabilities | SmartFill (assisted form-filling) and Formalize IQ (agoverned AI assistant / agent) |
| AI models | Anthropic Claude, accessed through Amazon Bedrock (anAWS-managed service) |
| Processing location | EU only: the platform is hosted in Frankfurt, Germany,model inference uses Amazon Bedrock EU inference profiles, and the AI tooling runs in AWS Frankfurt and AWS Ireland |
| Retention at the AI layer | Zero data retention: prompts and completions are not stored or logged by the AI service, and no AWS operator can access them. The only exception is a prompt cache that expires after 5 minutes (see Storage and Retention) |
| Training on customer data | Never: no training, no fine-tuning, and no Formalize-specific models. The AI services opt-out policy is enabled across our entire AWS organisation |
| Sub-processors | None added: AI processing is performed by AWS under the existing data processing agreement |
| Encryption | TLS 1.2 or higher in transit; AES (256 bit) at rest |
| Tenant isolation | All AI processing is scoped to a single organisation and bound by the requesting user's permissions |
| Human oversight | All AI output is reviewed by a human; data-modifying agent actions require explicit approval; no automated decision-making |
| Agent tool use | Formalize IQ: every tool call is permission-checked; changes to data require explicit human approval and are recorded |

| Web search | Formalize IQ can look up public sources through an AWS-managed search service in AWS Ireland: searches are answered from Amazon's own web index and pages are read from Amazon's cache of the web, so no request reaches a third-party search engine or the public internet, and only the search phrase or page address is sent. Can be switched off per organisation |
| Customer control | AI can be disabled organisation-wide in the platform, or fully removed on request; web search can additionally be switched off on its own |
| Usage limits | Enforced per organisation before any processing starts |
| Monitoring | Continuous monitoring with automated anomaly detection and real-time alerting |
| Security testing | Annual external penetration test, with prompt injection against Formalize IQ in scope |
| Auditability | Changes to AI settings, agent conversations, and every action performed via AI are recorded in the activity log |
| EU AI Act | Assessed against Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; not classified as high-risk |
| Certifications | ISO 27001 certified; annual ISAE 3000 Type 2 audits |

## 4 Customer Control: Disabling AI

The use of AI is entirely the customer’s choice, and the platform is fully usable without it:
every AI capability is an optional addition, and no part of the product depends on it. Disabling
AI applies to the organisation as a whole and covers every AI capability at once: SmartFill,
Formalize IQ, and any AI capability we release in the future. AI can be disabled at two levels, and one capability - web search - can additionally be switched off on its own:

• Organisation setting: administrators can disable AI for the whole organisation at any time,
directly from the platform settings. With the setting disabled, the AI capabilities cannot
be used by anyone in the organisation.

• Full removal: on request to our support team, we remove the AI feature from the organisation entirely. The AI capabilities are then no longer shown in the platform at all, and it
is not possible for anyone in the organisation - including administrators - to enable them.
Only Formalize can assign the feature again.

• Web search setting: administrators can switch off Formalize IQ’s ability to look up public
web sources, while leaving the rest of the AI capabilities available. With the setting off, no
web lookup is performed for the organisation at all, and the agent is told that web lookups
are unavailable so that it answers from the organisation’s own records instead.

None of these settings is just a user interface option - all of them are enforced server-side and
verifiable:

• Server-side enforcement: every AI request is checked in our backend against both the
organisation’s AI feature and its AI setting before any processing starts. When AI is
disabled at either level, AI requests are rejected, and no data is ever sent to Amazon
Bedrock on behalf of the organisation. The web search setting is enforced the same
way: it is checked on every single lookup, before any lookup is performed.

• Audited changes: every change to an organisation’s AI settings is recorded in the audit
log, including who changed the setting and when.

• Verifiable usage: AI usage (documents, form fields, tokens processed, and web searches
run) is tracked per organisation and displayed transparently on the AI settings page,
making it verifiable that no AI processing has taken place while AI is disabled.

## 5 SmartFill

SmartFill helps users fill out forms by reading documents the user selects (for example, a
contract PDF already uploaded to the platform) and suggesting values for the form fields the
user chooses. SmartFill processes only the selected documents and the definitions of the
selected form fields, and is a one-shot extraction: there is no conversation and no history built
up between requests.

Every suggested value is accompanied by a justification that explains where in the document
the value was found and why it was chosen. The user stays in control and can review, correct,
verify, or discard every suggestion.

## 6 Formalize IQ

Formalize IQ is an AI assistant that works across your live governance, risk, and compliance
program. Unlike SmartFill, which performs a single one-shot extraction, Formalize IQ is agentbased (see Definitions): it completes multi-step tasks by calling a set of well-defined tools - for
example, looking up records the user has access to, or drafting a new record - always acting
on behalf of the requesting user and always within that user’s permissions. It only ever runs
when a user starts a conversation with it; it never acts in the background.

Within a conversation, Formalize IQ can:

• Analyse your program: run a gap analysis against major frameworks (ISO 27001, SOC
2, NIS2, GDPR, and NIST) or review your risk register - grounded in your live data rather
than a generic checklist - and answer questions about your workspace, citing the records
it relied on.

• Draft and connect records: when a user explicitly asks, it drafts and links core records -
such as suppliers, contracts, processes, incidents, systems, assets, and business functions - for review. Every change is staged for the user’s approval before anything is
written.

• Build dashboards and charts: assemble dashboards and charts on request, staged for
approval like every other change.

• Work with your files: read spreadsheets, PDFs, Word documents, presentations, and
plain data files - both files a user attaches to the conversation and files already held in
the workspace, such as a document stored on a supplier - to compute over them or to produce a new file, for example filling in the answers to an .xlsx security questionnaire
from the organisation’s own records. The code it writes runs in an isolated sandbox, and
the original file is never altered (see Working with Files below).

• Look up public sources: search the public web for material that is not in your workspace -
the text of a regulation or standard, a supervisory authority’s guidance, public information
about a third party you are assessing - and read the pages it finds. Every claim it takes
from the web is shown with a link to its source. Both the search and the page reading are
served inside AWS, and the capability can be switched off on its own (see Web Search
below).

• Work transparently: it streams its reasoning, the records it inspects, and the actions it
proposes in real time, so users see why it does something, not just what it did.

### 6.1 Governed Tool Use

• Permission-checked tool usage: every tool call an agent makes is validated against the
requesting user’s permissions before it runs, using the same permission and tenantisolation checks that apply everywhere else in the platform. An agent can never read or
change anything the user could not read or change themselves, and it can only ever act
on data belonging to the user’s own organisation.

• Human-in-the-loop approvals: any tool that creates or modifies data pauses and requires
the user’s explicit approval before it runs; read-only tools change nothing and run without
a prompt. For each request the user can approve the single action, approve that tool for the rest of the conversation, or decline - and every decision is recorded together with the
user who made it and the time it was made.

• Full auditability: the complete conversation - every message, the records inspected, each
tool call, and its result - is persisted. Changes made by an agent are additionally recorded
in the activity log of every affected record, marked as performed via AI and attributed to
the user on whose behalf the agent acted and the conversation the change originated
from.

• Budgets and cancellation: agents run with hard limits on the number of steps and tokens
they may consume in a single run, in addition to the per-organisation usage limits described under Usage Limits and Monitoring. A user can cancel a running agent at any
time, and cancellation takes effect mid-run.

### 6.2 Working with Files: Sandboxed Code Execution

When Formalize IQ needs to compute - for example, to extract the questions from an .xlsx
security questionnaire, answer them from the organisation’s records, and write the answers
into a new copy of the file - it writes code and runs it in a sandbox provided by Amazon Bedrock
AgentCore, an AWS-managed service. The sandbox is built so that the code can do nothing
except compute over the files it was given:

• Isolated and network-restricted: each run executes in its own dedicated virtual machine
in AWS Frankfurt, with memory and a file system isolated from every other run, in AWS’s
most restrictive network mode. There is no route to the public internet, to our network, to
the platform, or to your database, and the sandbox holds no credentials of any kind, so
the code cannot call the agent’s tools or act on your workspace.

• Only the files it was given: the sandbox sees nothing but copies of the files the agent
explicitly hands it, each of which the requesting user must already have access to - the same permission check that applies to every other tool. No other workspace data is
present.

• Originals are never altered: the sandbox works on copies, so a run can only produce a
new file, never change or delete the one it read. Its only result is the printed output and
any new files, which are stored in the platform under the same permissions, encryption,
and audit trail as the rest of your data, for the user to review and download, and which
remain subject to the permission checks and human approvals described above.

• Single-use and bounded: every run starts on a clean sandbox with nothing carried over
from earlier runs, is limited by a hard execution timeout and by caps on the size and
number of files it may read and write, and is torn down when the run ends, at which point
AWS destroys the virtual machine and sanitises its memory. No code, data, or state
persists.

### 6.3 Web Search

Web search is the one capability that reaches outside your workspace. It is built so that as little
as possible leaves the workspace, nothing leaves AWS, and everything that comes back can
be checked:

• What is sent: a single search phrase of at most 200 characters, composed by the agent
for the question at hand. The phrase will often name what the user is working on - the
supplier being assessed, the standard being checked - but no record, document, or file
is ever transmitted with it.

• Where it runs: the search is performed by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore’s managed web
search service in AWS Ireland (eu-west-1), served from a web index that Amazon builds
and operates itself. The request is never handed to a third-party search engine and never
leaves AWS. This is an AWS service used under the same agreement as the rest of our
AWS usage, so it introduces no new sub-processor.

• What comes back: short text snippets, each with its source link and, where available,
its publication date. The search is strictly read-only: it retrieves public material and can
change nothing, in your workspace or anywhere else.

• Reading a page: when a snippet is not enough, the agent can open a page the search
returned and read its text. The page is served by the same AWS-managed tooling from
Amazon’s cache of the web; only the address of the page is sent, and no workspace
data accompanies it. AWS also offers a mode in which a page missing from the cache
is fetched live from the external web. We keep that mode disabled, in both the tool
configuration and our AWS permissions, because it is the one path by which a request
could leave AWS. A page Amazon has not cached therefore cannot be opened, and the
agent works from the snippet alone. Page content is treated as untrusted (see Resilience
to Prompt Injection below).

• Every claim is cited: Formalize IQ must attach the source to every claim it takes from the
web, and the interface shows the link, the domain, the publication date, and the exact
passage the claim rests on, so a reviewer can check the answer against the original.

• Under your control: web search can be switched off per organisation while the rest of
the AI capabilities stay available, the setting is checked on every single lookup before it
is performed, and each organisation has its own web search allowance (see Customer
Control and Usage Limits).

### 6.4 Resilience to Prompt Injection

Formalize IQ reads content it did not write - documents, form answers, files, and web pages -
and any of it could carry hidden instructions intended to manipulate the agent (see Definitions).
The safeguards are layered so that no single one has to hold. Content retrieved from outside
the workspace, above all web results and web pages, is presented to the agent as untrusted
data rather than instructions, and the agents are explicitly instructed to disregard any directive
found inside it, carry on with the user’s task, and report the attempt to the user.

That instruction is a first line of defence rather than a guarantee, which is precisely why the
controls around it are structural and hold regardless of what the model is persuaded to attempt: the agent cannot exceed the requesting user’s permissions, data-modifying actions still
require explicit human approval, tool inputs are validated against strict typed schemas, any
code execution stays confined to the sandbox, and writes execute in a single database transaction that is rolled back on any error. Together these layers provide defence in depth against
prompt-injection attacks.

Prompt injection against Formalize IQ, including attempts to use it to exceed the requesting
user’s permissions or to bypass the approval step, is within the scope of our annual external penetration test. The most recent report is available upon request.

### 6.5 In Development

Further capabilities are in development and not yet available. Each is assessed against the
controls in this document, and against the EU AI Act, before it is released, and all are covered
by the same organisation-wide AI setting:

• Automated setup: standing up and configuring a new environment automatically - the
way records are captured and connected, the reminders and workflows, who reviews
and signs off, and how risk is scored - matched to how the organisation actually works.

• Employee access from their own tools (MCP): exposing Formalize’s tools over a Model
Context Protocol (MCP) server, so employees can complete tasks, submit evidence, and
read policies from the AI tools they already use, such as Claude Code or OpenAI Codex.
Each user is authorised through OAuth 2.0, and every tool call is handled exactly as if
Formalize IQ had invoked it in the platform: scoped to that user, checked against their
permissions, confined to their organisation, and recorded in the audit trail. The one
difference is the human approval step for data-modifying actions, which is enforced by
the external tool according to its own configuration (for example, Claude Code’s toolapproval settings) rather than by Formalize’s own interface.

## 7 Processing and Infrastructure

All AI inference is performed through Amazon Bedrock, an AWS-managed service that runs
Anthropic’s Claude models entirely within AWS infrastructure. Our backend communicates directly with Amazon Bedrock, and customer data is never sent to the model provider (Anthropic)
or to any other third party:

• Model invocations use Amazon Bedrock EU inference profiles, which guarantee that AI
processing happens exclusively within AWS regions located in the EU. No data is transferred outside the EU/EEA in connection with the AI capabilities.

• Amazon Bedrock operates the models entirely within AWS. Using the AI capabilities
therefore does not introduce any new sub-processor: the processing is performed by
AWS, which already hosts the platform and is covered by our data processing agreement
and sub-processor list. The model provider has no access to requests or responses.

• Two Formalize IQ capabilities use AWS-managed tooling alongside the models, and both
stay inside AWS. Code execution runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore’s code interpreter
in Frankfurt (eu-central-1), the same region as the rest of the platform. Web search runs
through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore’s managed web search service in Ireland (eu-west-
1), the EU region in which AWS offers it: searches are answered from a web index that
Amazon operates itself, and pages the agent opens are served from Amazon’s cache of
the web, so no request is handed to a third-party search engine and our infrastructure
never opens a connection to the public internet. AWS offers a mode in which pages
missing from the cache are fetched from the external web; we keep it disabled. All of these are AWS services used under the same agreement as the rest of our AWS usage,
so none of them introduces a new sub-processor.

• All communication with Amazon Bedrock, including the AWS tooling described above, is
TLS encrypted and authenticated with AWS credentials, just like all other internal service

## 8 Data Lifecycle

The table below traces AI data through every stage - from the request a user makes to final
deletion - showing where each stage happens, how it is encrypted, and how long anything is
retained.

| Stage | Location | Encryption | Retention |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | User's browser to the Formalize platform; AWS Frankfurt (eu-central-1) | TLS 1.2+ in transit | Transient: assembled from records already in the platform; no separate copy is created |
| Inference | Amazon Bedrock, EU inference profile (AWS EU regions only) | TLS 1.2+ in transit; processed inside AWS | Not stored or logged by the model service; not used for training; only a prompt cache that expires after 5 minutes (see Storage and Retention) |
| Code execution | AWS-managed sandbox, AWS Frankfurt (eu-central-1) | TLS 1.2+ in transit; isolated virtual machine per run | Nothing persists. The sandbox works on copies, which are destroyed with it when the run ends and its memory is sanitised. Files the run produces are stored in the platform (below) |
| Web lookup | AWS-managed web search, AWS Ireland (eu-west-1); served from Amazon's index and cache inside AWS | TLS 1.2+ in transit | Only a short search phrase, or the address of a page to open, is sent - no record, document, or file; both are answered from Amazon's index and cache inside AWS. The query and its results are kept with the conversation (below) |
| Streaming | AWS IoT (MQTT) messaging, eu-central-1, to the user's browser | TLS in transit | Transient delivery only; the persisted copy lives in the database (below) |
| Storage | Primary database and file storage, AWS Frankfurt | AES (256 bit) at rest | Kept alongside your other records, under the same tenant isolation and retention rules |
| Backup | AWS, multiple availability zones, Frankfurt | AES (256 bit) at rest | Daily backup expires after 35 days; weekly backup after 85 days |
| Deletion | Database, file storage, and backups (Frankfurt) | Not applicable | Removed with the associated records via the platform's hard-delete process; purged from backups as they expire |

## 9 Storage and Retention

Amazon Bedrock operates under what AWS terms a zero data retention and zero operator access model: prompts (the data we send to the model) and completions (the output of the model)
are not written to durable storage, are not logged, cannot be accessed by AWS operators, and
are never used to train any model. The only exception is a short-lived performance cache: to
speed up follow-up requests within a conversation, Amazon Bedrock may hold prompt content
in an encrypted, temporary cache scoped to our AWS account. Each cache entry expires automatically after 5 minutes, is never used for training, and is not shared with the model provider
or any other party. Beyond this transient cache, no customer data remains within the AI service
once a request has been processed.

The AI output and records that we do store - such as SmartFill’s suggested values and their
justifications, and Formalize IQ conversations together with their tool calls and results - are
stored in our primary database in Frankfurt, Germany, alongside the rest of your data. This
data is encrypted at rest using AES (256 bit), included in regular backups, subject to the same
tenant isolation, and follows the same retention and deletion rules as all other customer data.

Both capabilities read data that is already stored in the platform; no additional copies of documents or records are created for AI purposes. What an AI capability can add to storage is
files: those a user attaches to a Formalize IQ conversation, and those Formalize IQ produces
on request, such as a filled-in questionnaire. Both are stored like any other file in the platform,
under the same encryption, tenant isolation, and retention rules. The sandbox that produced a
file keeps nothing once the run has ended.

## 10 No Training on Customer Data

Customer data is never used to train AI models: not by Formalize, not by AWS, and not by
the model provider. Amazon Bedrock contractually guarantees that prompts and completions
are not used to improve any models and are not shared with model providers or any other
third parties. In addition, the AI services opt-out policy is enabled across our entire AWS
organisation, which instructs every AWS AI service not to store or use our content to develop
or improve its services - a guarantee that covers all of our AWS accounts, not only Amazon
Bedrock.

The models are static from our perspective: nothing is learned or remembered between requests, and no data can leak from one customer to another through a model.

Formalize does not train, fine-tune, or otherwise modify the models. There is no Formalizespecific model: every request is processed by an unmodified foundation model. The specific
model in use is pinned in our codebase, so it is only ever changed through our standard,
reviewed change-management process, including code review and testing.

## 11 Tenant Isolation and Access Control

All AI processing is scoped to a single organisation. AI capabilities can only access data
belonging to the organisation of the user who triggered them, enforced by the same tenant isolation that applies to the rest of the platform.

In addition, AI capabilities act on behalf of the requesting user and are bound by the platform’s
granular permission structure: the AI can never read data that the requesting user would not
be able to read themselves.

## 12 Human Oversight

The AI capabilities in Formalize are built to assist users, never to act on their own. AI output is always presented for a human to review, and a human makes the final decision. For
SmartFill, every suggested value can be inspected (including the AI’s justification), corrected,
or discarded before the form is submitted. For Formalize IQ, answers are grounded in the
records the agent retrieved, and any action that changes data is additionally guarded by an
explicit user approval before it runs, as described under Formalize IQ.

AI never runs in the background: a capability only runs when a user explicitly invokes it, and
AI-generated suggestions are clearly marked as AI-generated in the user interface until a user
has reviewed them. No fully automated decisions are made, and nothing outside the platform
is changed without a human acting on it first.

## 13 Usage Limits and Monitoring

Every organisation has usage limits for AI, covering the number of documents and form fields
processed, the number of web searches run, as well as the total token consumption. The limits
are set and managed by Formalize per organisation and are enforced before processing starts,
preventing runaway usage. Formalize IQ agents additionally run with hard per-run limits on the
number of steps and tokens they may consume, and can be cancelled by the user at any time.

On the infrastructure side, all AI usage is continuously monitored with automated anomaly
detection on invocation volume, token consumption, errors, and throttling. Deviations alert our
engineering team in real time.

## 14 EU AI Act

Formalize has assessed its AI capabilities against Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the EU AI Act).
SmartFill is a document data-extraction utility: it reads documents selected by the user and
suggests values for form fields, with all output subject to mandatory human review before
any action is taken. Formalize IQ is an assistant that retrieves and explains information from
the user’s own workspace and from public web sources, computes over the user’s files, and
proposes records and changes for the user to accept: it surfaces information and drafts actions,
but every action that changes data requires explicit human approval before it takes effect, and
the user remains the decision-maker.

Neither capability performs profiling, makes automated decisions producing legal or similarly
significant effects on individuals, or falls within any of the use cases listed in Annex III of the
AI Act. On that basis Formalize assesses both as not high-risk. Users are clearly informed that they are interacting with AI and its output is labelled as AI-generated, addressing the
transparency considerations of Article 50. As a result, Formalize considers that the more
stringent requirements of Chapters III and IV of the AI Act apply neither to Formalize as provider
nor to the customer as deployer.

Roles and responsibilities under the AI Act are distributed as follows:

• Formalize (provider): integrates the AI capabilities into the platform and places them on
the market under its own product name, acting as provider of an AI system per Article
3(3) of the AI Act.

• Anthropic and AWS (model developer and service provider): the underlying Claude models are general-purpose AI models developed by Anthropic and operated by AWS as
a managed service (Amazon Bedrock). Obligations that apply to the underlying models, including those for general-purpose AI models under the AI Act, rest with the model
developer and the service operator.

• Customer (deployer): puts the platform into operation within its organisation, acting as
deployer per Article 3(4) of the AI Act. As the capabilities are assessed as not high-risk,
the specific obligations of Chapters III and IV do not apply to the customer as deployer.

Any future AI capability is assessed against the AI Act in the same way before it is released.

## 15 Known Limitations

In the interest of transparency, the following inherent limitations of the AI capabilities are disclosed:

• Extraction accuracy: AI-generated suggestions may be incorrect or incomplete, for example with low-quality scanned documents, ambiguous clauses, or domain-specific terminology. Every suggestion therefore includes a justification, and all suggestions must
be reviewed by a human before use.

• Language support: the underlying models support a broad but finite set of languages,
and extraction quality may vary between languages.

• Agent judgement: Formalize IQ can make mistakes in what it retrieves, concludes, or
proposes. Its answers should be verified against the records it cites, and because every
data-modifying action requires human approval, the reviewing user is responsible for
confirming that a proposed change is correct before approving it.

• Public web sources: material retrieved from the web comes from pages that Formalize
neither controls nor endorses, and it may be outdated, incomplete, or simply wrong.
Formalize IQ links the source of every claim it takes from the web precisely so that users
can check it against the original, and web results are never a substitute for legal advice
or for the organisation’s own records.
